problem: The service could not scale to monitor thousands of streams affordably.
title: Prime Video moves a monitoring service from distributed components to a single process
context: A video quality monitoring service built from distributed serverless components hit scaling limits and high cost.
decision_made: Rebuild it so components run together inside a single service on EC2/ECS instead of across separate serverless parts.
action_taken: Removed intermediate S3 storage for frames and orchestrated components within one instance.
observed_outcome: The team reported infrastructure cost reductions of over 90 percent for this service.
lessons: For a tightly coupled, high-throughput workload, fewer network hops can matter more than fine-grained decomposition.
limitations: Applies to one internal service, not Prime Video overall. Commentators disputed whether the result is truly a monolith. The primary post was not read directly; figures come from secondary coverage.

claims.claim_text: The team moved the monitoring workload to a single-service design on EC2 and ECS.
Operational cost for this service was reported as reduced by about 90 percent.
